feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications role: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows real scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with strong career progression at NACo and a well-aligned headline/profile.  
- Good credibility through concrete platforms, tools, and scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).  
- Writing is generally concise and professional, with strong domain relevance in advocacy, public-sector, and cross-channel communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable impact on engagement, efficiency, adoption, revenue, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a clearer leadership/value proposition would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current senior positioning and outcomes: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Reduce broad channel lists unless needed; emphasize cross-channel leadership, governance, and translating policy/technical issues for stakeholders.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The long channel list is repeated in multiple work experience entries.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and consistent singular/plural style; change “Multi-channel communication” to “Multichannel communications.”
- Prioritize higher-value leadership areas over task-level items like “Web & CMS administration.”
- Consider: Digital strategy & transformation • Editorial systems & governance • Web platform modernization • Multichannel communications leadership • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & automation • Stakeholder & cross-functional alignment • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- If space allows, swap in one more senior differentiator such as “AI-enabled search & content discovery” or “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the summary.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level while technical tools remain elsewhere.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the “Recent Projects” section. Tighten it around scope, ownership, and outcomes, and let projects carry some of the feature-level detail.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, content operations, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 4 concise, outcome-oriented bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics + governance/usability into one “improved cross-channel communications operations” bullet.
- Replace feature lists with impact framing: “Built Drupal campaign experiences and member resource hubs” instead of listing microsites, modules, and toolkits.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishers enabled, workflow time reduced, search relevance gains, engagement/conversion improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI-enabled search, microsites, anniversary campaign, and advocacy video already appear in “Recent Projects”; avoid repeating those specifics here.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also echo the NACo role—emphasize what is new/current in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and distinguish clearly from the earlier NACo roles, which already cover day-to-day channel management and video programming.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Prioritize the biggest wins first and make results explicit: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Rephrase channel oversight to show strategic impact, not just management: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials, strengthening advocacy distribution and audience engagement.”
- Tighten operations bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version more strategic.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries; focus here on building the studio/capability, not producing recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier digital/media role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and the build-out of repeatable editorial/video operations.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong theme fit, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and work experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinct value rather than repeating generic communications phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less redundant wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for high-volume publishing
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered planning & messaging
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel operating models” if you want a more systems/operations-forward tone.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this category to scale from recent roles (e.g., 10,000+ pages, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views) rather than keeping it purely generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages

- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the most marketable/recent items first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Remove lower-priority platforms here if they already appear in Technical + IT; keep this section selective, not exhaustive.
- If space allows, replace generic “Power Pages”/“SharePoint” with stronger positioning like “enterprise web platforms” unless those are target-role keywords.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages are already listed in Technical + IT, so avoid duplicating the full platform inventory here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and decision-making impact over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • Leadership reporting • Web performance and SEO analysis • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- Put strategic skills first; keep tools grouped at the end to signal seniority.
- Replace “KPI design” with “KPI framework design” and “SEO and performance analysis” with “Web performance and SEO analysis” for clearer, stronger phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, such as “analytics infrastructure” or “decision-support reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; avoid repeating the same tool stack in both places.
- “Leadership reporting” also overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery environment and production scope rather than repeating broad video terms.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level and relevance: “Drupal (primary enterprise CMS) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, group by strength: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, SharePoint, Power Pages • Publishing platforms: WordPress, GitHub Pages”
- Prioritize recent, high-impact tools first; Drupal should clearly lead given the recent 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- If you can substantiate it elsewhere, add scope in parentheses, e.g., “Drupal (migration, microsites, governance)” rather than just naming tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; consider deleting one version or making this one more technical/proficiency-based.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms unless it supports a specific project or portfolio use case.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and the more current tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API and tag implementation • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value for a senior candidate.
- Consider replacing “API integrations” with “API integration and workflow automation” only if you want to reinforce hands-on systems work not already covered elsewhere.
- Keep newer, differentiating tools like Cloudflare Workers and GitHub Actions; they signal modern technical execution better than jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- “Workflow automation” is already covered elsewhere, so don’t overstate it here unless tied to a specific tool.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems
- Group by function for faster scanning: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied use: “workflow design, task orchestration, cross-team collaboration”
- Consider trimming to the strongest/recent tools most tied to current work; keep Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira/Asana, Slack/Teams and drop weaker/older items if space is tight

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar project-management tools; listing all four may feel padded unless each was used meaningfully

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a vendor list rather than a skills statement. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused without repeating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/strength signal instead of more tools: Enterprise email campaign management • newsletter operations • audience segmentation
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was light exposure, remove it to strengthen credibility

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience growth,” or campaign leadership language here; that is already covered in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” may overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms” is more precise.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it read as the foundation-building role: team formation, early platform/process improvements, and hands-on production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete contributions: specify the website refresh, volume/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, or any audience/reach metrics if available.
- Tighten the ending to show leadership without overstating: “Mentored a digital media associate on daily production, publishing and content coordination.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while mentoring a digital media associate on day-to-day production and publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating generic workflow language already used in later NACo entries unless you can add specifics.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support and the podcast as a distinct first.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities, while contributing digital and multimedia content across organizational communications.”
- Make the podcast a separate, sharper clause: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specific outputs if known: web articles, audio segments, interview prep, multimedia assets, stakeholder research.
- Add any measurable scope if available: number of episodes launched, audiences served, programs supported, or cross-team partners.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating later-role language about “digital communications operations,” “video updates,” or team leadership.
- Keep this focused on innovation/research coordination and first-podcast creation, not general multimedia management.
